domain_title: Human impact, rights, fairness, transparency, oversight and recourse
title: Human and fundamental-rights impact
canonical_definition: The organization evaluates direct, indirect and cumulative benefits and harms for users, non-users, affected groups and rights across the actual context.

conditions: All systems affecting people; formal impact assessment depends on role, jurisdiction and consequence.
Record the assessed release, operating scope and evidence that supports any applicability decision.

primary_questions.question: Are affected persons, rights, benefit-harm pathways, severity, likelihood, reversibility and vulnerability defined?
Are impact mitigations, stakeholder input, escalation and review integrated into design and operation?
Do evaluation and post-deployment evidence show impacts are monitored, mitigated and reassessed after change?

conditions: Refer a material failure of human and fundamental-rights impact to the accountable authority before a consequential transition.

normative_source_mappings.relevant_locator: NIST AI 100-1, MAP 5.1 (PDF p. 32), MAP 5.2 (PDF p. 33), MEASURE 4.2 (PDF p. 36)
normative_source_mappings.mapping_rationale: The voluntary framework provides guidance on identifying impacts, engaging relevant actors and evaluating trustworthiness in context. The SAE criteria define the object-specific rules. Confirm any binding obligation through the accountable authority and its applicable source.

governance_purpose: Make human and fundamental-rights impact verifiable against the current AI system, decision context and accountable ownership.
distinct_claim: E1 evaluates human and fundamental-rights impact using evidence from intent through operation. AP-E1 independently assesses evidence of user-only impact framing.

atomic_subcriteria.criterion: The versioned definition identifies an impact map linking affected people, including non-users and vulnerable groups, to harms, benefits, severity and reversibility. Record the accountable owner, scope and material assumptions.
The current release demonstrates design controls, affected-group consultation, review routes and ongoing monitoring tied to the impact map. Trace the decisions and controls to attributable records.

Representative, executed evidence provides representative group and pathway results with monitoring and reassessment after material changes. Compare expected and observed outcomes and record exceptions.
For an operating system, current records cover the material paths involved in human and fundamental-rights impact, including relevant exceptions and changes.

required_evidence.title: Versioned scope and control definition
required_evidence.description: Provide an impact map linking affected people, including non-users and vulnerable groups, to harms, benefits, severity and reversibility. Include the affected workflow, current version and accountable owner.

required_evidence.title: Effective implementation records
required_evidence.description: Demonstrate design controls, affected-group consultation, review routes and ongoing monitoring tied to the impact map. Trace the scope, control and authority to the current implementation, including exceptions.

required_evidence.title: Representative verification results
required_evidence.description: Provide representative group and pathway results with monitoring and reassessment after material changes. Include current version, test scope, criteria, expected and observed outcomes, and unresolved failures.

required_evidence.title: Current operating or change evidence
required_evidence.description: Retain dated records that show how human and fundamental-rights impact works for the assessed scope, including the relevant exceptions and any material change since the evidence was captured.

sufficiency: Start with an impact map linking affected people, including non-users and vulnerable groups, to harms, benefits, severity and reversibility. Reconcile it against the effective controls and representative results for the same operating scope and version.

Use representative group and pathway results with monitoring and reassessment after material changes to support effectiveness at the relevant lifecycle stage. Record missing paths and unresolved conflicts as UNKNOWN. A verified shortfall can support a gap without resolving the other questions.
Reassess affected evidence after a material change. An accountable human validates or approves the result where required by the lifecycle target.
evidence_rules.evidence_ceiling: A specification supports DECLARED intent. Effective implementation records may support IMPLEMENTED. Representative executed tests support TESTED within their scope. Current operating evidence supports OPERATIONALLY_OBSERVED for covered paths and time. Record human assurance independently.
false_positive_guards: A proportionate assessment may use representative consultation where exclusions and limitations are justified and reviewable.
Reconcile document claims with the effective release, actual operation and relevant exceptions before recording satisfaction.
prohibited_inferences: A capability gap alone cannot establish AP-E1 presence.
An approved design or evidence plan cannot establish test execution or operational effectiveness.
Satisfying this capability cannot by itself authorize progression or establish legal compliance.

finding_definitions.title: Material definition or intent gap in human and fundamental-rights impact
Verified implementation or effectiveness gap in human and fundamental-rights impact
Evidence remains insufficient for human and fundamental-rights impact in the assessed scope
